messages.subject: (Fwd) Re: Models with no adjustments
parts:
Your analysis sounds OK. I would suggest doing some comparative
analyses with a larger truncation distance, just to check that the results
are consistent. The issues of size bias are all familiar - especially
with those of us who have spent too much time in International Whaling
Commn meetings. In fact, the regression methods in DISTANCE handle these
sources of bias quite adequately, provided estimates of size are OK close
to zero. The slope can sometimes go the 'wrong' way, due to
underestimation of size of distant groups. If this is suspected, then
keep the correction. (In fact, I wonder whether we should change DISTANCE
so that we don't discourage people from using the regression when the
slope has the wrong sign ...) The problem of cluster definition affects
the shape of the detection function, but provided a regression method of
correcting size bias is used (preferably the default method), this doesn't
cause bias. It DOES cause bias of course if you just estimate mean size
by the mean size of recorded groups - we need a good estimate of mean size
AT ZERO DISTANCE.

Steve Buckland
